category: Structural material models II: plasticity, creep, viscoplasticity, porous/soil/concrete/rock plasticity and damage
description: Inelastic material subnodes of the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module and Geomechanics Module: yield criteria and hardening laws, creep laws, (polymer) viscoplasticity, porous plasticity, soil and critical-state models, concrete and rock models, and damage/fracture models. Type strings and parameter keys were checked in COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: von Mises and Tresca Yield Criteria (Plasticity)
tools.description: The Plasticity subnode adds rate-independent elastoplasticity to Linear Elastic, Nonlinear Elastic or Hyperelastic Material in Solid Mechanics, Shell, Layered Shell, Membrane and Truss. The default equivalent stress is von Mises with associated flow (J2 plasticity for metals); Tresca uses the maximum shear stress with an associated (smoothed) or von Mises plastic potential; User defined accepts any expression of stress invariants. The initial yield stress sigma_ys0 is taken from the Elastoplastic material model property group.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Plasticity. Java: feature("lemm1").create("plsty1", "Plasticity", 3); feature("lemm1").feature("plsty1").set("YieldFunction", "mises" | "hill" | "userDefined"); material group ElastoplasticModel (sigmags, Et, Ek, sigmagh, Hillcoefficients, ys).

parameters.name: YieldFunction
parameters.description: mises (default), Tresca, hill or userDefined (sigmagf expression).

parameters.name: sigmags
parameters.description: Initial yield stress sigma_ys0 (From material or User defined).

parameters.name: FlowPotential / Qplast
parameters.description: associated or userDefined plastic potential (non-associated flow).

parameters.name: equivalentStrain / hp
parameters.description: How the equivalent plastic strain is computed: associated, mises or user defined.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module (or Geomechanics Module for some options). An Equivalent Plastic Strain result template (solid.epe) is added. Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Plasticity/elastoplastic_plate. Local return mapping settings (Backward Euler, damped) are under Advanced.

tools.name: Hill Orthotropic Plasticity (Plasticity)
tools.description: Hill's quadratic anisotropic yield criterion for rolled sheet metals, extrusions and textured materials. Anisotropy is specified by the initial tensile and shear yield stresses in the principal directions, by Hill's coefficients F, G, H, L, M, N, or by the dimensionless coefficients f..n; the directions follow the parent material's coordinate system. Equivalent plastic strain can be associated or von Mises based.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Plasticity > Equivalent stress = Hill orthotropic. Java: set("YieldFunction", "hill"); set("HillPlasticityOptions", "ys" | "Hillcoefficients"); set("equivalentStrainHill", "associated" | "mises").

parameters.name: HillPlasticityOptions
parameters.description: ys (six initial tensile/shear yield stresses sigma_ys0ij) or Hillcoefficients (F, G, H, L, M, N); dimensionless variant also available.

parameters.name: ys / Hillcoefficients
parameters.description: Six-component vectors, From material (ElastoplasticModel group) or User defined.

parameters.name: Initial yield stress
parameters.description: sigma_ys0 or the Reciprocal average yield stress for Hill's criterion.

tools.notes: Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Plasticity/orthotropic_container and orthotropic_container_shell (orthotropic elasticity + Hill plasticity).

tools.name: Perfectly Plastic and Linear Isotropic Hardening (Plasticity)
tools.description: Simplest hardening options: Perfectly plastic keeps the yield stress constant (ideal plasticity, limit-load analysis); Linear raises the yield stress proportionally to the equivalent plastic strain using the isotropic tangent modulus E_Tiso, i.e. sigma_ys = sigma_ys0 + E*E_T/(E - E_T)*eps_pe (bilinear stress-strain curve).
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Plasticity > Isotropic hardening model = Perfectly plastic | Linear. Java: set("IsotropicHardeningModel", "PerfectlyPlastic" | "LinearIsotropicHardening"); tangent modulus Et in the ElastoplasticModel group.

parameters.name: IsotropicHardeningModel
parameters.description: PerfectlyPlastic or LinearIsotropicHardening.

parameters.name: Et
parameters.description: Isotropic tangent modulus E_Tiso (slope of the plastic branch in a uniaxial test).

tools.notes: Perfect plasticity can lose uniqueness at the limit load; use load or displacement control with an auxiliary sweep and stop at the collapse load.

tools.name: Ludwik and Swift Power-Law Hardening (Plasticity)
tools.description: Nonlinear isotropic hardening laws of power type. Ludwik: sigma_ys = sigma_ys0 + k*eps_pe^n (strength coefficient k, hardening exponent n). Swift: sigma_ys = sigma_ys0*(1 + eps_pe/eps0)^n with reference strain eps0, typically eps0 = sigma_ys0/E. Both are common for sheet-metal forming data.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Plasticity > Isotropic hardening model = Ludwik | Swift. Java: set("IsotropicHardeningModel", "Ludwik"); material groups Ludwik (k_lud, n_lud) and Swift (e0_swi, n_swi).

parameters.name: k_lud, n_lud
parameters.description: Ludwik strength coefficient and hardening exponent.

parameters.name: e0_swi, n_swi
parameters.description: Swift reference strain and hardening exponent.

tools.notes: Ludwik with n < 1 has infinite initial slope at eps_pe = 0, which can slow convergence; Swift avoids that.

tools.name: Voce and Hockett-Sherby Saturation Hardening (Plasticity)
tools.description: Exponential saturation laws for metals whose hardening levels off. Voce: sigma_ys = sigma_ys0 + sigma_sat*(1 - exp(-beta*eps_pe)) with saturation flow stress and saturation exponent. Hockett-Sherby: sigma_ys = sigma_inf - (sigma_inf - sigma_ys0)*exp(-m*eps_pe^n) with steady-state flow stress, saturation coefficient m and exponent n.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Plasticity > Isotropic hardening model = Voce | Hockett-Sherby. Java: set("IsotropicHardeningModel", "Voce"); material groups Voce (sigma_voc, beta_voc) and HockettSherby (sigma_hoc, m_hoc, n_hoc).

parameters.name: sigma_voc, beta_voc
parameters.description: Voce saturation flow stress and saturation exponent.

parameters.name: sigma_hoc, m_hoc, n_hoc
parameters.description: Hockett-Sherby steady-state flow stress, saturation coefficient and exponent.

tools.notes: Voce is also available in Viscoplasticity; combine with Armstrong-Frederick kinematic hardening for cyclic plasticity (Lemaitre-Chaboche type models).

tools.name: Johnson-Cook Hardening (Plasticity)
tools.description: Strain-rate and temperature dependent hardening used for impact, crash, machining and forming: sigma_ys = (sigma_ys0 + k*eps_pe^n)(1 + C*ln(rate/rate0))*(1 - f(Th)). Modified Johnson-Cook changes the rate term. Thermal softening can be None, Power law (reference and melting temperature, exponent m) or a User defined function of the homologous temperature <phys>.<mat>.<plsty>.Th.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Plasticity > Isotropic hardening model = Johnson-Cook | Modified Johnson-Cook. Java: set("IsotropicHardeningModel", "JohnsonCook"); set("ThermalSoftening", "PowerLaw" | "NoThermalSoftening"); material group JohnsonCook (k_jcook, n_jcook, C_jcook, epet0_jcook, m_jcook).

parameters.name: k_jcook, n_jcook
parameters.description: Strength coefficient and hardening exponent.

parameters.name: C_jcook, epet0_jcook
parameters.description: Strain-rate strength coefficient and reference strain rate (default 1e-3 1/s).

parameters.name: ThermalSoftening, Tref, Tm, m_jcook
parameters.description: Thermal softening model, reference and melting temperature, temperature exponent.

tools.notes: Rate dependence needs a Time Dependent or Explicit Dynamics study. Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Plasticity/strain_rate_dependent_plasticity and phone_drop_test. Couple with Heat Transfer and the Adiabatic Heating node for thermal softening from plastic work.

tools.name: Hardening Function (Plasticity)
tools.description: Arbitrary isotropic hardening curve sigma_h(eps_pe) added to the initial yield stress, usually an interpolation function of measured true stress versus plastic strain. The function must be zero at zero plastic strain and may depend on temperature or other variables. This is the most common way to import tensile-test data.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Plasticity > Isotropic hardening model = Hardening function. Java: set("IsotropicHardeningModel", "HardeningFunction"); ElastoplasticModel property sigmagh (e.g. an interpolation function of solid.epe).

parameters.name: sigmagh
parameters.description: Hardening function sigma_h(eps_pe), e.g. int1(solid.epe) or max(0, curve(solid.epe + solid.mises/solid.E) - solid.sigmags).

tools.notes: Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Plasticity/elastoplastic_plate (second part uses a measured curve) and temperature_dependent_plasticity.

tools.name: Linear and Armstrong-Frederick Kinematic Hardening (Plasticity)
tools.description: Kinematic hardening translates the yield surface by a back stress to capture the Bauschinger effect in cyclic loading. Linear (Prager) uses a kinematic tangent modulus Ek with back stress collinear to the plastic strain. Armstrong-Frederick adds a recall term, d(sigma_b) = Ck*d(eps_p) - gamma_k*sigma_b*d(eps_pe), giving saturating back stress and ratcheting. Both can be combined with any isotropic hardening (mixed hardening).
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Plasticity > Kinematic hardening model = Linear | Armstrong-Frederick. Java: set("KinematicHardeningModel", "LinearKinematicHardening" | "ArmstrongFrederick" | "NoKinematicHardening"); material groups ElastoplasticModel (Ek) and ArmstrongFrederick (Ck, gammak).

parameters.name: Ek
parameters.description: Kinematic tangent modulus for linear (Prager) hardening.

parameters.name: Ck, gammak
parameters.description: Armstrong-Frederick kinematic hardening modulus and parameter (saturation back stress Ck/gammak).

tools.notes: Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Plasticity/biomedical_stent (Armstrong-Frederick). The Set Variables node can reset the back strain tensor.

tools.name: Chaboche Kinematic Hardening (Plasticity)
tools.description: Multi-branch nonlinear kinematic hardening: the total back stress is the sum of N Armstrong-Frederick back stresses plus an optional linear term C0, each branch with hardening modulus C_i and parameter gamma_i. It reproduces cyclic stress-strain loops, ratcheting and mean-stress relaxation of metals much better than a single branch and is the basis for low-cycle fatigue analyses.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Plasticity > Kinematic hardening model = Chaboche; fill the branch table (Hardening modulus, Hardening parameter). Java keys: C_cha, gamma_cha (branch data), Ck0_cha (linear modulus C0).

parameters.name: C0 (Ck0_cha)
parameters.description: Linear kinematic hardening modulus.

parameters.name: Branch table
parameters.description: C_i (Pa) and gamma_i per branch; loadable from a three-column text file.

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material 1 > Plasticity 1
Isotropic hardening model: Voce, Kinematic hardening model: Chaboche
Branches: (C1 = 150 GPa, gamma1 = 1500), (C2 = 20 GPa, gamma2 = 150), (C3 = 2 GPa, gamma3 = 0)
Study: Time Dependent with a cyclic prescribed displacement
tools.notes: The corresponding viscoplastic form is the Chaboche viscoplasticity model. Enable energy dissipation in the parent node to post-process plastic work per cycle for energy-based fatigue.

tools.name: Implicit Gradient Nonlocal Plasticity (Plasticity)
tools.description: Regularization of the equivalent plastic strain by an implicit gradient (Helmholtz-type) equation that removes mesh dependence in softening or localizing problems such as necking, shear bands and soil failure. The nonlocal strain is coupled to the local one with a length scale l_int (larger than the element size) and a coupling modulus H_nl (about 10 % of the shear modulus). Also available in Soil Plasticity, Porous Plasticity and Pressure-Dependent Plasticity.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Plasticity > Nonlocal Plasticity Model = Implicit gradient. Java: set("nonlocalPlasticModel", "impGradient"); set("lint", ...); set("hnl", "1e-1*solid.Gequ").

parameters.name: nonlocalPlasticModel
parameters.description: none or impGradient.

parameters.name: lint
parameters.description: Regularization length scale.

parameters.name: hnl
parameters.description: Nonlocal coupling modulus (default 0.1*solid.Gequ).

tools.notes: Adds a dependent variable for the nonlocal plastic strain (shape function under Discretization). Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Plasticity/bar_necking.

tools.name: Annealing (Plasticity)
tools.description: Subnode to Plasticity that resets the hardening variables (equivalent plastic strain and back stress) whenever the temperature exceeds a specified annealing temperature, emulating recrystallization in welding, heat treatment or additive manufacturing simulations.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic / Nonlinear Elastic Material > Plasticity > Annealing.

parameters.name: Annealing temperature
parameters.description: Temperature above which plastic hardening variables are reset.

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material 1 > Plasticity 1 > Annealing 1
Annealing temperature: 0.6*T_melt
Temperature model input from Heat Transfer in Solids (ht)
tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module. For general conditional resets use Set Variables.

tools.name: Set Variables (Plasticity, Creep and Soil Models)
tools.description: Subnode that resets internal state variables of an inelastic model to user values when a Boolean setting condition becomes true: equivalent plastic/creep/viscoplastic strain, the plastic strain tensor, back strain (kinematic hardening) and porosity rate. It is used for staged processes, e.g. removing plastic history after machining or mapping strains from a previous forming step.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Plasticity / Creep / Viscoplasticity / Porous Plasticity / Soil Plasticity / Concrete / Rocks / Elastoplastic Soil Material > Set Variables. Java: feature("lemm1").feature("plsty1").create("setv1", "SetVariables", 2).

parameters.name: Setting condition
parameters.description: Boolean expression, e.g. t>1[s].

parameters.name: Equivalent plastic strain / Plastic strain tensor
parameters.description: Do not set or User defined (default 0).

parameters.name: Back strain tensor / Porosity rate
parameters.description: Extra variables for kinematic hardening and porous plasticity.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("solid").feature("lemm1").feature("plsty1").create("setv1", "SetVariables", 2);
// Setting condition: t>t_unload, Equivalent plastic strain: User defined = epe_mapped(x,y)
tools.notes: Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Plasticity/plastic_strain_mapping.

tools.name: Pressure-Dependent Plasticity (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Plasticity for pressure-sensitive materials such as polymers, foams, powders and adhesives. Models: Drucker-Prager (sigma_ys0 and pressure parameter a1, optional non-associated a1Q), Elliptic (b1, b2, b3 shape in the meridional plane with Circular, Gudehus or Lagioia-Panteghini octahedral section), Foam (crushable foam with volumetric hardening) and Parabolic (a1..a4). Can be combined with Cap and Cutoff and with Linear Elastic, Nonlinear Elastic or Hyperelastic parents.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Pressure-Dependent Plasticity. Java: feature("hmm1").create("pdpl1", "PressureDependentPlasticity", 3); set("plasticityModel", "foam"); material groups PressureDependentPlasticity (a1yield..a4yield, b1yield..b3yield) and FoamPlasticity (pc0, pch, pt, sigmauc0, sigmauch, nup).

parameters.name: plasticityModel
parameters.description: Drucker-Prager, elliptic, foam or parabolic.

parameters.name: plasticPotential
parameters.description: associated or nonassociated.

parameters.name: octahedralSection
parameters.description: circular, Gudehus (strength ratio c) or Lagioia-Panteghini (c1, c2, c3).

parameters.name: Foam: pc0, pt, sigmauc0, nup, pch
parameters.description: Initial hydrostatic compression yield, tensile limit, uniaxial compressive yield, plastic Poisson's ratio and volumetric hardening function.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module. For soils prefer Soil Plasticity; for powders Porous Plasticity.

tools.name: Norton (Creep)
tools.description: Power-law secondary creep, creep rate = A*(sigma_e/sigma_ref)^n, the most widely used model for steady-state creep of metals at high temperature. Combined with the Time hardening option it gives the Norton-Bailey primary creep law (rate multiplied by (t/t_ref)^m), and with Strain hardening its strain-hardening equivalent. The equivalent stress can be von Mises, Hill orthotropic, pressure or user defined.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Creep > Material model = Norton. Java: feature("lemm1").create("cmm1", "Creep2", 3); feature("lemm1").feature("cmm1").set("materialModel", "Norton"); material group Norton (A_nor, sigRef_nor, n_nor).

parameters.name: A_nor
parameters.description: Creep rate coefficient A (1/s).

parameters.name: sigRef_nor
parameters.description: Reference stress (default 1 MPa).

parameters.name: n_nor
parameters.description: Stress exponent n.

parameters.name: equivalentStress
parameters.description: mises, Hill orthotropic, pressure or user defined.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module or Geomechanics Module. Adds an Equivalent Creep Strain template (solid.ece). Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Creep/turbine_stator_creep and combined_creep.

tools.name: Garofalo Hyperbolic Sine (Creep)
tools.description: Creep rate = A*sinh(sigma_e/sigma_ref)^n, which behaves like a power law at low stress and exponentially at high stress; it covers the power-law breakdown regime and is used for solders and high-temperature alloys. Usually combined with Arrhenius thermal effects.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Creep > Material model = Garofalo (hyperbolic sine). Java: set("materialModel", "Garofalo"); material group Garofalo (A_gar, sigRef_gar, n_gar).

parameters.name: A_gar
parameters.description: Creep rate coefficient.

parameters.name: sigRef_gar
parameters.description: Reference stress (default 1 MPa).

parameters.name: n_gar
parameters.description: Stress exponent.

tools.notes: Application Library: Fatigue_Module/Energy_Based/surface_mount_resistor (creep of solder feeding energy-based fatigue).

tools.name: Nabarro-Herring and Coble Diffusion Creep (Creep)
tools.description: Physically based linear (Newtonian) diffusion creep laws for low stress and high temperature: Nabarro-Herring (lattice diffusion, volume diffusivity Dv) and Coble (grain-boundary diffusion, diffusivity Dgb), both defined by the Burgers vector b and grain diameter d. Coble dominates in fine-grained materials and at lower temperatures.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Creep > Material model = Nabarro-Herring | Coble. Java parameter keys: D_nav, b_nav, dg_nav (Nabarro-Herring) and D_cob, b_cob, dg_cob (Coble).

parameters.name: Dv / Dgb
parameters.description: Volume or grain-boundary diffusivity (m^2/s).

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: Burgers vector length.

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Grain diameter.

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material 1 > Creep 1
Material model: Coble, Dgb = 1e-14[m^2/s], b = 0.25[nm], d = 5[um]
Thermal Effects: Arrhenius, Q = 150[kJ/mol]
tools.notes: Several creep mechanisms can be summed with Additional Creep subnodes (e.g. Coble + Norton dislocation creep).

tools.name: Weertman (Creep)
tools.description: Dislocation climb creep law with diffusivity D, Burgers vector b, stress exponent n and reference stress, giving a physically motivated power-law creep rate. Useful when diffusion data rather than fitted Norton constants are available.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Creep > Material model = Weertman. Java parameter keys: D_wee, b_wee, n_wee, sigRef_wee.

parameters.name: D_wee
parameters.description: Diffusivity.

parameters.name: b_wee
parameters.description: Burgers vector.

parameters.name: n_wee, sigRef_wee
parameters.description: Stress exponent and reference stress (1 MPa).

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material 1 > Creep 1
Material model: Weertman, D = 1e-18[m^2/s], b = 0.286[nm], n = 4.5, sigma_ref = 1[MPa]
tools.notes: User defined creep rate f(sigma_e) is available for any other law, with default <creep node>.sequ/1[Pa*s].

tools.name: Creep Hardening and Thermal Effects (Creep)
tools.description: Every creep law is multiplied by a hardening function h and a thermal function g. Hardening: None, Strain hardening (exponent m, strain shift, reference time), Time hardening (exponent m, time shift, reference time) or User defined, which turns secondary laws into primary creep (e.g. Norton-Bailey). Thermal: None, Arrhenius (activation energy Q, reference temperature, Inf by default) or User defined. Time stepping of the creep equations is Automatic, Backward Euler, Forward Euler or Domain ODEs.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Creep > Isotropic Hardening Model / Thermal Effects / Time Stepping. Java: set("isotropicHardening", "none" | "time" | ...); set("thermalEffects", "none" | "Arrhenius"); set("timeMethod", "automatic" | "forwardEuler").

parameters.name: isotropicHardening, m, tRef, tShift, eceShift
parameters.description: Hardening function type and its exponent, reference time and shifts.

parameters.name: thermalEffects, Q, T0
parameters.description: Arrhenius activation energy and reference temperature.

parameters.name: timeMethod, maxit, abstol, reltol, maxec
parameters.description: Local integration method and tolerances (maximum creep strain increment for forward Euler).

tools.notes: Forward Euler requires resetting solver defaults; Backward Euler is not available in Layered Shell. See Solver Settings for Viscoelasticity, Creep, and Viscoplasticity for time-step advice.

tools.name: Additional Creep (Creep)
tools.description: Subnode to Creep that adds another creep mechanism whose strain rate is summed with the parent law, for example primary plus secondary creep, or diffusion plus dislocation creep. It has the same model choices (Norton, Garofalo, Nabarro-Herring, Coble, Weertman, User defined) and can inherit the equivalent stress from the parent.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Creep > Additional Creep. Java: feature("lemm1").feature("cmm1").create("acr1", "AdditionalCreep", 3); set("equivalentStress", "fromParent").

parameters.name: materialModel
parameters.description: Creep law of the additional mechanism.

parameters.name: equivalentStress
parameters.description: fromParent or its own definition.

tools.notes: Application Library: Fatigue_Module/Strain_Life/accelerated_life_testing.

tools.name: Anand (Viscoplasticity)
tools.description: Unified viscoplastic model without an explicit yield surface, in which a scalar deformation resistance s evolves with the viscoplastic strain rate. It is the standard model for lead-free solder joints in thermal cycling. Parameters: rate coefficient A, activation energy Q (via material), stress multiplier xi, stress sensitivity m, saturation coefficient s_sat, initial resistance s_init, hardening coefficient h0, hardening sensitivity a and resistance sensitivity n. Anand-Narayan is a variant with the same inputs.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Viscoplasticity > Material model = Anand. Java: feature("lemm1").create("vpl1", "Viscoplasticity", 3); set("ViscoplasticityModel", "Anand"); material group Anand (A_ana, Q_ana, xi_ana, m_ana, ssat_ana, sa_init, h0_ana, a_ana, n_ana).

parameters.name: A_ana, Q_ana
parameters.description: Viscoplastic rate coefficient and activation energy.

parameters.name: xi_ana, m_ana
parameters.description: Stress multiplier and strain-rate sensitivity.

parameters.name: ssat_ana, sa_init, h0_ana, a_ana, n_ana
parameters.description: Deformation resistance saturation, initial value, hardening coefficient, hardening sensitivity and resistance sensitivity.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module. Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Viscoplasticity/viscoplastic_solder_joints and Fatigue_Module/Energy_Based/viscoplastic_solder_joints_fatigue.

tools.name: Chaboche (Viscoplasticity)
tools.description: Overstress viscoplasticity with rate lambda_vp = A*(<sigma_e - sigma_ys>/sigma_ref)^n, combined with any isotropic hardening (e.g. Voce) and kinematic hardening (Armstrong-Frederick/Chaboche). Together these form the Lemaitre-Chaboche unified model for cyclic, rate-dependent metal behavior at elevated temperature.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Viscoplasticity > Material model = Chaboche. Java: set("ViscoplasticityModel", "Chaboche"); set("IsotropicHardeningModel", "Voce"); set("KinematicHardeningModel", "ArmstrongFrederick"); material group ChabocheViscoplasticity (A_cha, sigRef_cha, n_cha).

parameters.name: A_cha, sigRef_cha, n_cha
parameters.description: Viscoplastic rate coefficient, reference stress, stress exponent.

parameters.name: YieldFunction, sigmags
parameters.description: Equivalent stress (von Mises, Tresca, Hill, user) and initial yield stress.

parameters.name: IsotropicHardeningModel / KinematicHardeningModel
parameters.description: Hardening laws as in Plasticity.

tools.notes: Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Viscoplasticity/lemaitre_chaboche_viscoplastic_model.

tools.name: Perzyna, Peric and Bingham (Viscoplasticity)
tools.description: Further overstress viscoplastic laws with a yield surface: Perzyna (rate coefficient A and reference stress, linear overstress), Peric (rate coefficient A and stress exponent n, a variant that behaves better at high rates) and Bingham (viscosity eta, viscous flow above yield, e.g. for pastes). A User defined equivalent viscoplastic rate is also possible. All support the full choice of yield criteria and hardening models.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Viscoplasticity > Material model = Perzyna | Peric | Bingham | User defined. Java parameter keys: A_per, n_per (Perzyna), A_peric, n_peric (Peric), eta_bing (Bingham), lambdavp (user).

parameters.name: Perzyna: A, sigma_ref
parameters.description: Rate coefficient and reference stress (1 MPa).

parameters.name: Peric: A, n
parameters.description: Rate coefficient and stress exponent.

parameters.name: Bingham: eta
parameters.description: Viscosity (default 1 Pa s).

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material 1 > Viscoplasticity 1
Material model: Perzyna, A = 1e-3[1/s], sigma_ref = 10[MPa]
Plasticity Model: von Mises, sigma_ys0 = 250[MPa], Isotropic hardening: Linear
tools.notes: For rate-independent limits use Plasticity; viscoplastic models regularize the solution and often converge more robustly.

tools.name: Bergstrom-Boyce (Polymer Viscoplasticity)
tools.description: Large-strain viscoplastic network added in parallel to a Hyperelastic Material for elastomers: a spring (energy factor beta_v times the parent stiffness) in series with a nonlinear dashpot with rate coefficient A, flow resistance, stress exponent n and cutoff stress, plus optional strain hardening. It captures rate dependence, hysteresis and relaxation of rubbers.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Polymer Viscoplasticity > Material model = Bergstrom-Boyce. Java: feature("hmm1").create("pvp1", "PolymerViscoplasticity", 3); set("ViscoplasticityModel", "BergstromBoyce"); material group BergstromBoyce (A_BB, sigRes_BB, n_BB, c_BB, sigmaco_BB).

parameters.name: betav
parameters.description: Energy factor of the network spring (default 1.2).

parameters.name: A_BB, sigRes_BB, n_BB
parameters.description: Viscoplastic rate coefficient, flow resistance, stress exponent.

parameters.name: c_BB, sigmaco_BB
parameters.description: Strain-hardening exponent and cutoff stress.

parameters.name: StaticResponse
parameters.description: Long-term or Instantaneous stiffness in stationary studies.

tools.notes: Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Viscoplasticity/chloroprene_rubber_compression_test and parameter_estimation_polymer_viscoplasticity. Thermal effects (Arrhenius, power law) scale the rate.

tools.name: Bergstrom-Bischoff (Polymer Viscoplasticity)
tools.description: Two viscoplastic networks in parallel with the hyperelastic equilibrium network, designed for thermoplastics such as HDPE and UHMWPE: pressure-dependent flow resistance in both networks and an evolving energy factor in the second network model yielding, strain softening and large-strain flow.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Polymer Viscoplasticity > Material model = Bergstrom-Bischoff. Java: set("ViscoplasticityModel", "BergstromBischoff"); material group BergstromBischoff (A_BeBi, sigRes1_BeBi, sigRes2_BeBi, n1_BeBi, n2_BeBi, a1_BeBi, a2_BeBi).

parameters.name: A_BeBi
parameters.description: Viscoplastic rate coefficient.

parameters.name: betav1, sigRes1, n1, a1
parameters.description: First network energy factor, flow resistance, stress exponent, pressure hardening.

parameters.name: betav2_i, betav2_f, alpha, sigRes2, n2, a2
parameters.description: Second network initial/final energy factor and evolution, flow resistance, exponent, pressure hardening.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module; large plastic strain kinematics are used.

tools.name: Parallel Network (Polymer Viscoplasticity)
tools.description: Generic parallel rheological framework: one or more spring-dashpot networks in parallel with a hyperelastic parent, where each spring can inherit the parent (energy factor) or use its own Neo-Hookean, Mooney-Rivlin, Yeoh, Ogden, Arruda-Boyce or Gent law, and each dashpot has rate coefficient, flow resistance, exponent, cutoff stress, pressure hardening and strain hardening. Extra networks are added with Additional Network subnodes.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Polymer Viscoplasticity > Material model = Parallel network; right-click to add Additional Network. Java parameter keys: HyperelasticMaterialPN, betavPN, A_PN, sigRes_PN, n_PN, sigmaco_PN, a_PN, c_PN.

parameters.name: Spring material model
parameters.description: From parent, Neo-Hookean, Mooney-Rivlin, Yeoh, Ogden, Arruda-Boyce or Gent.

parameters.name: Dashpot parameters
parameters.description: A, flow resistance, exponent n, cutoff stress, pressure hardening a.

parameters.name: Isotropic hardening
parameters.description: None, Strain hardening (exponent c) or User defined.

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material 1 (Arruda-Boyce) > Polymer Viscoplasticity 1
Material model: Parallel network, spring From parent (beta_v = 2)
> Additional Network 1: beta_v = 0.5, A = 1[1/s], flow resistance 2[MPa], n = 4
tools.notes: Parameter estimation from test curves: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Viscoplasticity/parameter_estimation_polymer_viscoplasticity.

tools.name: Gurson and Gurson-Tvergaard-Needleman (Porous Plasticity)
tools.description: Porous metal plasticity in which the yield surface depends on the void volume fraction, so hydrostatic tension grows voids and leads to ductile fracture. Gurson needs the initial yield stress and initial void fraction f0; GTN adds Tvergaard coefficients q1, q2, q3 and an effective void fraction (Bilinear or Asymptotic with critical fc and failure ff). Void nucleation in tension and void growth in shear can be enabled.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Porous Plasticity > Material model = Gurson | Gurson-Tvergaard-Needleman. Java: feature("lemm1").create("popl1", "PorousPlasticity", 3); set("YieldFunction", "GTN"); material group PoroplasticModel (sigmags, f0, q1GTN, q2GTN, q3GTN, fc, ff, fn, snn, enn, kw).

parameters.name: f0
parameters.description: Initial void volume fraction.

parameters.name: q1GTN, q2GTN, q3GTN
parameters.description: Tvergaard corrections (q3 = q1^2 by default).

parameters.name: EffectiveVoidFunction, fc, ff
parameters.description: Bilinear/Asymptotic coalescence acceleration with critical and failure void fractions.

parameters.name: VoidNucleation (fn, snn, enn) / VoidGrowthShear (kw)
parameters.description: Strain-controlled nucleation and Nahshon-Hutchinson shear growth.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module; adds Volumetric Plastic Strain and Current Void Volume Fraction templates. Use nonlocal regularization for softening.

tools.name: Shima-Oyane and Fleck-Kuhn-McMeeking (Porous Plasticity)
tools.description: Porous plasticity models for powder compaction and sintered materials. Shima-Oyane (parameters alpha, gamma, m) describes densification of metal powders; Fleck-Kuhn-McMeeking describes compaction at high relative density with a maximum void fraction f_max; FKM-GTN blends FKM and GTN between cutoff void fractions and can use an associated, GTN or FKM plastic potential.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Porous Plasticity > Material model = Shima-Oyane | Fleck-Kuhn-McMeeking | FKM-GTN. Material group PoroplasticModel (alphaShima, gammaShima, mShima, f0, fmax, ...).

parameters.name: alphaShima, gammaShima, mShima
parameters.description: Shima-Oyane parameters.

parameters.name: fmax
parameters.description: Maximum void volume fraction (FKM, FKM-GTN).

parameters.name: f_GTN, f_FKM
parameters.description: Void fraction cutoffs for switching between GTN and FKM (FKM-GTN).

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material 1 > Porous Plasticity 1
Material model: Shima-Oyane, sigma_ys0 = 100[MPa], alpha = 2.5, gamma = 1.8, m = 1, f0 = 0.4
Study: Stationary with an auxiliary sweep of punch displacement
tools.notes: Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Porous_Plasticity/powder_compaction_of_a_cup and two_stage_compaction.

tools.name: Capped Drucker-Prager (Porous Plasticity)
tools.description: Drucker-Prager shear failure line closed by a compression cap whose position hardens with volumetric plastic strain, the standard model for pharmaceutical tableting and ceramic/metal powder pressing. Inputs are the initial yield stress, yield parameter a1 (and a1Q for non-associated flow), initial void fraction and the Cap Model data (elliptic cap, exponential hardening, maximum volumetric plastic strain).
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Porous Plasticity > Material model = Capped Drucker-Prager. Java: set("YieldFunction", "DruckerPrager"); set("capHardeningModel", "exponential"); material groups PoroplasticModel and CapAndCutoff (pc0, pcc0, Kc, epvolmax).

parameters.name: sigmags, ayield, apotential
parameters.description: Initial yield stress and pressure parameters of the yield function and potential.

parameters.name: compressionCap, pc0, pcc0
parameters.description: Cap shape and initial pressure limit/centroid.

parameters.name: capHardeningModel, Kc, epvolmax
parameters.description: Perfectly plastic, linear, exponential or hardening function; hardening modulus; maximum volumetric plastic strain.

tools.notes: The octahedral section of this model is always circular.

tools.name: Drucker-Prager (Soil Plasticity)
tools.description: Cone-shaped pressure-dependent yield surface for soils, rock and concrete, defined by alpha and k or matched to Mohr-Coulomb cohesion c and friction angle phi (Compressive meridian, Tensile meridian, Inscribe for plane strain, Uniaxial or Biaxial plane stress). Associated or non-associated (dilatation angle psi) flow; optional hardening of cohesion and a Cap and Cutoff subnode.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Soil Plasticity > Failure criterion = Drucker-Prager. Java: feature("lemm1").create("sopl1", "SoilPlasticity", 2); set("failureCriterion", "DruckerPrager"); set("matchToMohrCoulomb", "inscribe"); material group Soil (cohesion0, phis, psis, ksoil0, asoil, aqsoil, ksoilh, cohesionh).

parameters.name: matchToMohrCoulomb
parameters.description: compressiveMeridian, tensile meridian, inscribe, uniaxial, biaxial or user defined (k0, alpha).

parameters.name: cohesion0, phis, psis
parameters.description: Initial cohesion, friction angle and dilatation angle.

parameters.name: plasticPotential
parameters.description: associated or nonassociated.

parameters.name: IsotropicHardeningModel
parameters.description: PerfectlyPlastic or hardening of k/cohesion (ksoilh, cohesionh).

tools.notes: Requires the Geomechanics Module. Application Library: Geomechanics_Module/Soil/flexible_footing and Geomechanics_Module/Verification_Examples/block_verification.

tools.name: Mohr-Coulomb (Soil Plasticity)
tools.description: Classical Mohr-Coulomb shear failure with cohesion and friction angle (hexagonal octahedral section, corners smoothed numerically). Flow can be associated, non-associated with a dilatation angle, or use a Drucker-Prager plastic potential for robustness. It is the default choice for slope stability, excavations, footings and tunnel linings.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Soil Plasticity > Failure criterion = Mohr-Coulomb. Java: set("failureCriterion", "MohrCoulomb"); set("plasticPotential", "associated" | "nonassociated" | Drucker-Prager).

parameters.name: cohesion0, phis
parameters.description: Initial cohesion and friction angle (Soil material group).

parameters.name: psis
parameters.description: Dilatation angle for the non-associated potential (or From friction angle).

parameters.name: plasticPotentialSmoothing, offsetVertex
parameters.description: Vertex smoothing of the plastic potential (Advanced).

tools.notes: Use a gravity load plus initial in situ stress (External Stress or Initial Stress and Strain) before excavation steps. Strength reduction (factor of safety) studies sweep c and tan(phi) (Geomechanics_Module/Verification_Examples/strength_reduction_method).

tools.name: Matsuoka-Nakai and Lade-Duncan (Soil Plasticity)
tools.description: Smooth pressure-dependent criteria based on the first and third stress invariants that circumscribe the Mohr-Coulomb hexagon: Matsuoka-Nakai (matches Mohr-Coulomb at both triaxial compression and extension) and Lade-Duncan (cohesionless sands, matched at triaxial compression). They avoid the corner singularities of Mohr-Coulomb and are well suited for granular soils.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Soil Plasticity > Failure criterion = Matsuoka-Nakai | Lade-Duncan; Match to Mohr-Coulomb = Compressive meridian or User defined.

parameters.name: cohesion0, phis
parameters.description: Mohr-Coulomb parameters used for matching.

parameters.name: k0, alpha (user defined)
parameters.description: Direct Drucker-Prager-type parameters when not matched.

parameters.name: Plastic potential
parameters.description: Associated, Nonassociated (dilatation angle) or Drucker-Prager.

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material 1 > Soil Plasticity 1
Failure criterion: Matsuoka-Nakai, Match to Mohr-Coulomb: Compressive meridian
c0 = 5[kPa], phi = 35[deg], Plastic potential: Drucker-Prager with psi = 5[deg]
tools.notes: Matsuoka-Nakai is also an octahedral-section option of the Elastoplastic Soil Material (critical state models).

tools.name: Cap and Cutoff (Soil Plasticity)
tools.description: Subnode that closes open pressure-dependent yield surfaces. The compression cap can be Elliptic, Planar or Cam-clay with hardening Perfectly plastic, Linear, Exponential or Hardening function driven by volumetric or equivalent plastic strain; the tension cutoff can be a Mean stress limit or a Rankine principal-stress limit. Available under Pressure-Dependent Plasticity, Soil Plasticity and Elastoplastic Soil Material (Hardening Soil models).
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Soil Plasticity (or Pressure-Dependent Plasticity / Elastoplastic Soil Material) > Cap and Cutoff. Java: feature("epm1").create("cac1", "CapAndCutoff", 3); set("compressionCap", "elliptic"); set("capHardeningModel", "linear"); set("tensionCutoff", "none").

parameters.name: compressionCap, pc0, pcc0
parameters.description: Cap model and initial pressure limit / ellipse centroid.

parameters.name: capHardeningModel, Kc, epvolmax, capHardeningVariable
parameters.description: Cap hardening law, modulus, maximum volumetric plastic strain and hardening variable.

parameters.name: tensionCutoff, svolt / sigmaut
parameters.description: Mean stress limit or Rankine tensile strength.

parameters.name: plasticModelSmoothing, capSoftening
parameters.description: Intersection smoothing and optional cap softening in tension.

tools.notes: Application Library: Geomechanics_Module/Verification_Examples/triaxial_and_oedometer_test_hs (cap with Hardening Soil).

tools.name: Modified Cam-Clay (Elastoplastic Soil Material)
tools.description: Critical-state model for normally and lightly overconsolidated clays with an elliptic yield surface in p-q space whose size (preconsolidation pressure) hardens with volumetric plastic strain. Inputs are swelling index kappa, compression index lambda, slope of the critical state line M (or friction angle), initial void ratio and reference/preconsolidation pressures; elasticity is pressure dependent.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Material Models > Elastoplastic Soil Material > Material model = Modified Cam-clay. Java: physics("solid").create("epm1", "ElastoplasticSoilModel", 3); set("MaterialModel", "ModifiedCamClay"); material groups ModifiedCamClay (kappaSwelling, lambdaComp, evoidref) and CriticalStateModel (nu, G, M, Mq, internalphi, psid, evoid0).

parameters.name: kappaSwelling, lambdaComp
parameters.description: Swelling and compression indexes.

parameters.name: M / internalphi
parameters.description: Slope of the critical state line or friction angle (Match to Mohr-Coulomb).

parameters.name: pc0, pref, evoid0
parameters.description: Preconsolidation pressure, reference pressure, initial void ratio.

parameters.name: octahedralSection, plasticPotential
parameters.description: Circular, Mohr-Coulomb or Matsuoka-Nakai section; associated, nonassociated or McDowell-Hau potential.

tools.notes: Requires the Geomechanics Module. Add External Stress (pore pressure) for effective stress with Darcy's Law/Richards' Equation. Application Library: Geomechanics_Module/Verification_Examples/isotropic_compression and Geomechanics_Module/Soil/settlement_analysis.

tools.name: Modified Structured Cam-Clay (Elastoplastic Soil Material)
tools.description: Extension of Modified Cam-Clay for natural structured clays whose bonding (structure strength p_b0) degrades with plastic volumetric and shear deformation (destructuring indexes dv and ds). It captures the higher yield stress and subsequent collapse compression of undisturbed samples.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Elastoplastic Soil Material > Material model = Modified structured Cam-clay. Java: set("MaterialModel", "ModifiedStructuredCamClay"); material group ModifiedStructuredCamClay (kappaSwellings, lambdaCompd, evoidrefd, evoid0s, dv, ds, Deltaec0, pb0, zeta, edevepf).

parameters.name: kappaSwellings, lambdaCompd
parameters.description: Swelling index of structured clay and compression index of destructured clay.

parameters.name: pb0, dv, ds
parameters.description: Initial structure strength and destructuring indexes (volumetric, shear).

parameters.name: Deltaec0, edevepf, evoid0s
parameters.description: Additional void ratio at preconsolidation, plastic deviatoric strain at failure, initial void ratio.

tools.notes: Plastic potential McDowell-Hau is available for this family.

tools.name: Extended Barcelona Basic (Elastoplastic Soil Material)
tools.description: Critical-state model for unsaturated soils (BBM extension) where suction increases the apparent preconsolidation pressure and tensile strength; it predicts collapse on wetting and swelling on drying. Inputs include swelling/compression indexes at saturation and for suction changes, weight parameter w, soil stiffness parameter m, smoothing b, tension-to-suction ratio k and initial suction yield value.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Elastoplastic Soil Material > Material model = Extended Barcelona basic. Java: set("MaterialModel", "ExtendedBarcelonaBasic"); material group BarcelonaBasic (kappaSwelling0, kappaSwellingsu, lambdaComp0, lambdaCompsu, evoidref0, evoid0b, wb, mb, bb, kb, sy0).

parameters.name: kappa0, kappas, lambda0, lambdas
parameters.description: Indexes at saturation and for suction changes.

parameters.name: w, m, b, k, s_y0
parameters.description: Weight, stiffness, smoothing, tension/suction ratio and initial suction yield.

parameters.name: s0, s
parameters.description: Initial suction and current suction (e.g. from Richards' Equation).

tools.notes: Typically coupled to Richards' Equation through the suction input.

tools.name: Hardening Soil and Hardening Soil Small Strain (Elastoplastic Soil Material)
tools.description: Double-hardening soil models with stress-dependent stiffness (reference moduli E50/Ei, Eur at p_ref with exponent m), hyperbolic stress-strain response with failure ratio Rf, Mohr-Coulomb failure (c, phi) and mobilized dilatancy (Soreide, Rowe, Modified Rowe, Wehnert). The Small Strain variant adds the very stiff small-strain shear modulus G0 and its decay with reference shear strain gamma_ref, important for excavations and foundations.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Elastoplastic Soil Material > Material model = Hardening soil | Hardening soil small strain. Java: set("MaterialModel", "HardeningSoil" | "HardeningSoilSmall"); set("MobilizedDilatancyAngleOption", "Soreide" | "Rowe" | "ModifiedRowe"); material group HardeningSoil (EiRef, E50Ref, EurRef, G0, G0Ref, gammaRef, mh, cohesion).

parameters.name: EiRef/E50Ref, EurRef, mh
parameters.description: Reference stiffness for primary loading, unloading/reloading, and stress exponent.

parameters.name: G0 / G0Ref, gammaRef
parameters.description: Small-strain shear modulus and reference shear strain (small strain version).

parameters.name: cohesion, internalphi, Rf, pref
parameters.description: Strength parameters, failure ratio and reference pressure.

parameters.name: DilatancyCutOff, evoidm
parameters.description: Dilatancy cutoff with maximum void ratio.

tools.notes: Add Cap and Cutoff for the volumetric cap (preconsolidation pressure). Load reversal points for small-strain stiffness are Automatic by default.

tools.name: Coupled Damage-Plasticity (Concrete)
tools.description: Concrete model combining plasticity with separate tensile and compressive damage (in the spirit of CDPM2) for multiaxial and cyclic loading, including stiffness recovery and dilatancy. Inputs are tensile, compressive and biaxial compressive strengths, compressive yield stress, tension softening (Linear, Bilinear, Cornelissen, Exponential or user curves) and compression softening with fracture energies, regularized by the crack band method.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Concrete > Material model = Coupled damage-plasticity. Java: feature("lemm1").create("cm1", "Concrete", 3); set("materialModel", "coupledDamagePlasticity"); set("tensionSofteningCdpm", "bilinear" | "cornelissen"); material groups YieldStressParameters (sigmaut, sigmauc, sigmabc, sigmaucy) and FractureParameters (Gft, Gfc).

parameters.name: sigmaut, sigmauc, sigmabc, sigmaucy
parameters.description: Tensile, compressive, biaxial compressive strength and compressive yield stress (defaults 1.16 and 0.3 x fc).

parameters.name: tensionSofteningCdpm, Gft
parameters.description: Tension softening curve and tensile fracture energy.

parameters.name: compressionSofteningCdpm, Gfc, As_cdpm
parameters.description: Compression softening curve, compressive fracture energy and ductility parameter (default 10).

parameters.name: regularizationTensionCdpm, crackband_cdpm
parameters.description: Crack band or none; element volume/area or element size.

tools.notes: Requires the Geomechanics Module. Application Library: Geomechanics_Module/Concrete/concrete_beam_cdpm (with Embedded Reinforcement truss bars) and Verification_Examples/concrete_damage_plasticity.

tools.name: Mazars Damage (Concrete)
tools.description: Strain-based scalar damage model for concrete under monotonic loading with separate tensile and compressive damage evolution weighted by the stress state. Equivalent strain is Mazars, Modified Mazars or User defined; tensile evolution can be Linear, Exponential, Polynomial, Multilinear, Mazars function or user defined, with fracture-energy regularization. It is a computationally lean alternative to damage-plasticity.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Concrete > Material model = Mazars damage (also Damage > Mazars damage for concrete). Java: set("materialModel", "mazarsDamage"); set("equivalentStrainMazars", "mazars" | "modifiedMazars").

parameters.name: beta_maz
parameters.description: Shear exponent (default 1.06).

parameters.name: tensionDamageMazars, epsilonft_maz / Gft
parameters.description: Tensile damage evolution and softening input.

parameters.name: compressionDamageMazars, eps0c, Ac, Bc
parameters.description: Compressive threshold and Mazars evolution parameters.

tools.notes: Not suitable for cyclic loading (no plastic strains). Maximum damage (default 1-1e-5) keeps residual stiffness.

tools.name: Bresler-Pister, Willam-Warnke and Ottosen (Concrete Perfect Plasticity)
tools.description: Perfect plasticity option of the Concrete node: a multiaxial concrete failure surface without hardening, intended to check whether strength is reached. Bresler-Pister and Willam-Warnke use tensile, compressive and biaxial compressive strengths; Ottosen uses compressive strength, parameters a and b, size factor k1 and shape factor k2. An optional principal stress tension cutoff limits tensile stress.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Concrete > Material model = Perfect plasticity, Yield function = Bresler-Pister | Willam-Warnke | Ottosen. Java: set("materialModel", "perfectPlasticity"); set("ConcreteCriterion", "BreslerPister" | "Ottosen"); material group Ottosen (aOttosen, bOttosen, k1Ottosen, k2Ottosen).

parameters.name: sigmaut, sigmauc, sigmabc
parameters.description: Strengths for Bresler-Pister and Willam-Warnke.

parameters.name: aOttosen, bOttosen, k1Ottosen, k2Ottosen
parameters.description: Ottosen parameters.

parameters.name: SelectTensionCutoff, sigmattc
parameters.description: None or principal stress cutoff with maximum tensile stress.

tools.notes: The same criteria are also available as non-affecting Safety failure criteria.

tools.name: Hoek-Brown (Rocks)
tools.description: Rocks subnode with the empirical Hoek-Brown failure criterion for rock masses: Original Hoek-Brown (uniaxial compressive strength, m and s) or Generalized Hoek-Brown (compressive strength of intact rock, Geological Strength Index GSI, disturbance factor D and intact rock parameter m_i). An optional principal stress tension cutoff limits tensile stress. Used for tunnels, mines, rock slopes and blasting.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic / Nonlinear Elastic Material > Rocks > Material model = Original Hoek-Brown | Generalized Hoek-Brown.

parameters.name: sigma_cs, m, s
parameters.description: Original Hoek-Brown parameters.

parameters.name: GSI, D, m_i
parameters.description: Generalized Hoek-Brown rock mass parameters.

parameters.name: Tension cutoff
parameters.description: None or Principal stress cutoff with maximum tensile stress.

parameters.name: Local method
parameters.description: Automatic or Backward Euler with iteration limit and tolerance (Advanced).

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material 1 > Rocks 1
Material model: Generalized Hoek-Brown, sigma_cs = 80[MPa], GSI = 55, D = 0, m_i = 10
Study: Stationary with gravity and in situ stress, then excavation via Activation
tools.notes: Requires the Geomechanics Module. Adds an Equivalent Plastic Strain template.

tools.name: Scalar Damage (Damage)
tools.description: Isotropic strain-based damage for brittle and quasi-brittle materials: the stiffness is reduced by (1-d) where d grows with the maximum equivalent strain. Equivalent strain can be Rankine (stress or strain), Smooth Rankine, Norm of elastic strain tensor or User defined; damage evolution is Linear, Exponential, Polynomial, Multilinear strain softening or User defined, defined through tensile strength and fracture energy. Optional delayed-damage viscous regularization.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Damage > Damage model = Scalar damage. Java: feature("lemm1").create("dmg1", "Damage", 2); set("ModelType", "ScalarDmg"); set("scalarEquivStrain", "Rankine"); set("ScalarDmgEvo", "Exponential"); material group ScalarDamage (sigmap, Gf, gf).

parameters.name: scalarEquivStrain
parameters.description: Rankine, strain-based Rankine, smooth variants, elastic strain norm or user defined.

parameters.name: ScalarDmgEvo
parameters.description: Linear, Exponential, Polynomial, Multilinear or user defined.

parameters.name: sigmap, Gf / gf / epsf
parameters.description: Tensile strength and fracture energy per area/volume or softening strain.

parameters.name: viscRegType, tauv
parameters.description: None or Delayed damage with characteristic time.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials or Geomechanics Module. Always combine with a regularization method (crack band or implicit gradient) to avoid mesh dependence. Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Damage/damage_test_bar and notched_beam_damage.

tools.name: Phase-Field Damage (Damage)
tools.description: Brittle fracture by a diffuse crack phase field with length scale l_int that naturally handles crack initiation, branching and merging. Crack driving force: elastic or total strain energy density (critical energy release rate Gc, threshold), principal stress criterion (critical fracture stress, post-peak slope) or user defined; degradation Power law or Cubic (Borden); compressive energy exclusion by volumetric-deviatoric or spectral split. Also available for hyperelastic materials and via the Phase-Field Damage multiphysics interface.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic (or Hyperelastic) Material > Damage > Damage model = Phase-field damage. Java: set("ModelType", "PhaseFieldDmg"); set("phCrackDrivingForce", "energetic"); set("strainEnergySplit", "volDev"); material group PhaseFieldDamage (sigmacr, Gc, scrit).

parameters.name: phCrackDrivingForce
parameters.description: Elastic/total strain energy, principal stress criterion or user defined.

parameters.name: Gc, lint_ph
parameters.description: Critical energy release rate and phase-field length scale (mesh must resolve it).

parameters.name: phDmgFunction, m / s
parameters.description: Power law exponent (m = 2) or Borden cubic parameter.

parameters.name: strainEnergySplit
parameters.description: Volumetric only, spectral decomposition (stress/strain) or no split.

tools.notes: Mesh size should be about l_int/2 or smaller in the crack path. Use a segregated solver and small load increments.

tools.name: Crack Band and Implicit Gradient Regularization (Damage)
tools.description: Spatial regularization options that make softening damage results mesh-objective. Crack band scales the fracture energy by a characteristic element length (Element volume/area or Element size), keeping the dissipated energy per unit crack area constant. Implicit gradient solves an extra Helmholtz equation for a nonlocal equivalent strain with internal length l_int (and damage zone size h_dmg when fracture energy per area is used).
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Damage > Spatial regularization method = None | Crack band | Implicit gradient. Java: set("regType", "crackBand" | "impGradient"); set("crackBandDef", "volMethod"); set("lint", ...); set("hdmg", ...).

parameters.name: regType
parameters.description: crackBand or impGradient (none also possible).

parameters.name: crackBandDef
parameters.description: Element volume/area (volMethod) or element size.

parameters.name: lint, hdmg
parameters.description: Internal length scale and characteristic damage zone size (implicit gradient).

tools.notes: Implicit gradient is recommended with a mixed formulation parent; crack band works with only fracture energy per area as softening input.

tools.name: Test Material (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Global node that sets up and runs virtual material tests on a single-element specimen for the material model of one selected domain, to check stability and calibrate parameters before running the real model. Tests: Uniaxial, Biaxial, Shear, Isotropic, Oedometer and Triaxial, in a Stationary or Time dependent setup with Monotonic, Cyclic or User defined (stretch- or force-driven) loading. The Set Up and Run Tests button builds the studies and plots.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > (right-click) Test Material, select one domain, choose tests, click Set Up and Run Tests. Java: physics("solid").create("tm1", "TestMaterial", -1).

parameters.name: Specimen size
parameters.description: Automatic (1 m element) or User defined characteristic length.

parameters.name: Study setup / Test setup
parameters.description: Stationary or Time dependent; Monotonic, Cyclic (number of cycles) or User defined.

parameters.name: Tests
parameters.description: Uniaxial (lambda_min, lambda_max), Biaxial (ratio beta), Shear (angle), Isotropic, Oedometer, Triaxial (in situ stress).

parameters.name: Number of measurement points
parameters.description: Resolution of the generated sweep (default 50).

tools.notes: Useful for detecting unstable hyperelastic parameter sets (loss of Drucker stability) and for soil model verification (Geomechanics_Module/Verification_Examples/concrete_damage_plasticity).
